findings.location: Guide §1 High availability and disaster recovery, third paragraph
findings.evidence: The guide says protected applications are recovery groups. Oracle documents a Disaster Recovery or DR Protection Group as the consistency grouping that contains member resources: [Oracle DR Protection Group documentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/disaster-recovery/doc/overview-protection-groups.html).
findings.recommendation: Replace recovery groups with DR Protection Groups and describe applications and resources as group members; use the same terminology in related lab and readiness wording.

results.notes: Strong broad-scope guide, but the wrong name for a core Full Stack Disaster Recovery object requires correction.

findings.location: Guide paragraph beginning This is a fast-moving beta; §3 Retrieval, tools and identity; §4 Evaluate and deploy
findings.evidence: The official exam guide's in-scope list includes BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Firestore, Memorystore for Redis, Model Garden, and Google Cloud Observability. The guide has no substantive selection, role, or limitation coverage for these named services while calling its shorter enumeration the in-scope product list: [official exam guide](https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/professional_agentic_architect_exam_guide_english.pdf).
findings.recommendation: Add a compact decision map for every explicitly in-scope product, especially data stores, Model Garden, and Cloud Logging and Trace, or label the existing list non-exhaustive and point omitted tools to substantive coverage.

findings.location: Guide opening disclosure and Scheduled change line
findings.evidence: The guide remains verified September 2 and labels September 3 registration opening as scheduled. On September 4 the official page exposes Register, and the FAQ publishes registration through September 30, the September 8–30 exam window, late-October multiple-choice results, and late-October-to-December labs: [official beta FAQ](https://support.google.com/cloud-certification/answer/18080541?ref_topic=9433464).
findings.recommendation: Rebaseline the opening status and lifecycle table to the open registration state and published beta windows while retaining the general-availability volatility warning.

findings.evidence: The record says the explicit in-scope tool list is mapped, but the guide omits substantive coverage of multiple tools named on the official PDF's final page.
findings.recommendation: After repairing the guide, enumerate where each official tool is covered; until then, narrow the review note so it does not claim complete tool-list mapping.

results.notes: Architecture guidance is strong, but explicit beta tool scope and the post-September-3 lifecycle state require repair.

findings.location: Guide §2 EtherChannel and Hands-on evidence lab 3; §5 opening paragraph; §6 REST APIs paragraph
findings.evidence: Cisco v1.1 objective 2.4 requires Layer 2 and Layer 3 LACP EtherChannel, but the guide discusses access, trunk, and VLAN members and provides only a Resilient Layer 2 lab. Objective 5.2 requires security-program elements, but awareness, training, and physical access appear only in a list. Objective 6.5 names REST authentication types, but the guide only says authentication: [Cisco v1.1 topics](https://learningcontent.cisco.com/documents/marketing/exam-topics/200-301-CCNA-v1.1.pdf).
findings.recommendation: Add routed Layer 3 port-channel configuration, verification, and failure evidence; explain awareness, training, and physical-access program elements; and compare representative REST authentication types and boundaries.

findings.location: data/reviews.json review 200-301-2026-09-02-source-validation, objective_coverage; guide Hands-on evidence labs 1–8
findings.evidence: The record maps Network Access to labs 1 and 4–5 instead of access and STP labs 2–3; Security omits security lab 6 and cites 5 and 7–8; Automation omits automation lab 7 and cites 6 and 8. IP Connectivity and IP Services also include unrelated lab ranges.
findings.recommendation: Map Network Access to labs 2–3, IP Connectivity to 4, IP Services to 5, Security to 6, and Automation to 7; cite capstone 8 only where its stated evidence applies.

results.notes: The guide is version-aware and technically strong, but current-objective gaps and materially inaccurate review mappings require repair.
